newsitem.title: CHINA: Korea defector may be on China flight for Manila.
newsitem.headline: Korea defector may be on China flight for Manila.

text.p: A China Southern Airlines flight believed to be carrying North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop out of China took off on Tuesday morning from the southeastern port city of Xiamen for Manila, officials said.

Flight CZ379 took off nearly 40 minutes late, at 10.58 a.m. (0300 GMT) but this was not unusual, said an airline official in Xiamen. The official declined to specify whether Hwang was on board, saying he was not listed among economy class passengers and identities of VIP travellers could not be revealed.
"I can't say if he is on board," one airline official said. "And even if he is on board I wouldn't tell you."
The scheduled flying time to Manila was about two hours and 10 minutes.

A special flight left Beijing early on Tuesday amid reports North Korea's top ideologue had been spirited out of the South Korean mission in the Chinese capital where he had been sheltering for nearly five weeks.

The flight took off from a military airport on the outskirts of Beijing at 7 a.m. (2300 GMT) and arrived about two and a half hours later in the southeastern coastal city of Xiamen, aviation officials in Xiamen said.
The aircraft was carrying a passenger who would take a scheduled flight to Manila at about 10.20 a.m. (0220 GMT), one official said by telephone.
The passenger's route matched the one Hwang was expected to take when he ended weeks of diplomatic limbo at the centre of a diplomatic crisis between Beijing and the two rival Koreas.
